target_customer: Large employers hiring high volumes of frontline and hourly workers, such as retailers, restaurants and consumer goods firms
problem: High-volume frontline hiring is slow and impersonal, so candidates drop out and recruiters waste time screening and coordinating.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for an AI recruiting assistant that engages candidates by text and chat
product_category: Conversational AI recruiting for frontline workers

founders.name: Mateo Cavasotto
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch 2022 says he and Andres Arslanian volunteered for a microcredit NGO in Argentina, where they began thinking about technology for job access. Education not stated.

founders.name: Andres Arslanian
founders.background_notes: Named CTO by TechCrunch 2022 and founder on the YC page. Education not stated.

competitors.name: Fountain
competitors.what: Hiring and onboarding platform for gig and hourly workers
competitors.funding_then: $23M Series B in October 2019, total $34M, dated about seven months after the batch

technical_complexity.rationale: Conversational screening over text with integrations into applicant tracking systems needed natural language handling of messy messages in several languages, standard but with hard parts.

defensibility.rationale: Integrations with big employers' hiring systems and conversation data give mild lock in, but chatbot hiring tools were copyable and competitors existed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Rivals such as Fountain raised larger rounds, and Workday acquired Paradox in October 2025 per a search summary. No acquisition of Emi found.

market_need_then: Large employers hire thousands of hourly workers a year, and TechCrunch 2022 reports customers like Walmart, Burger King and Starbucks using Emi, showing real demand from large enterprise buyers.

branding.domain_note: Uses emilabs.ai, not a bare emi.com (source: company site URL).

identity.logo: A search summary of a profile says the logo was designed to feel trustworthy inside a text thread, page itself blocked
identity.mascot_or_character: Emi, the assistant persona candidates chat with
identity.visual_style: WhatsApp style chat demo on the site
identity.voice_and_tone: human, simple and fair, per the company description

branding.brand_signature: Emi as a named AI assistant candidates text
branding.community_and_virality: Company claims over 3 million people have talked with Emi, a self-reported figure.

brand_strength.rationale: A friendly persona name fits a text based product but there is little press about the brand and the name is confusable with similar names.

outcome_analysis: Emi raised a seed after YC and an $11M Series A in February 2022 led by Merus Capital and Khosla Ventures, bringing total raised to $13.3M, with customers like Walmart and Starbucks and annual recurring revenue tripling in 2021. It is still active with about 50 people and now sells AI agents mainly in Mexico. It shows a steady enterprise story, with the later outcome still open.
notes: TechCrunch states $13.3M total raised including a seed after YC, so the seed is implied at about $2.3M, while an aggregator lists $2M in 2019-08 (startupintros, one source, unverified), so the seed amount and investors are left null. Series A confirmed by TechCrunch and aggregator outlets. Competitors named in the 2022 TechCrunch article (AskNicely, SnapShift, Blink, Shiftsmart, When I Work, Fountain, Seasoned) are not used as they are dated three years after the batch. Fountain's source is dated October 2019, seven months after the batch, noted. The yespress page was blocked (403) and was used only through a search summary. Company site is now Spanish language and Mexico focused.
